rationale: Kaur and Gupta review names saffron among herbs and depressive symptoms generally; no verified stigma preparation or measured saffron depression comparison in indexed abstract; publisher body blocked 403.
Bej review abstract mentions saffron and constituents with depression and Parkinson separately, without a symptom-specific clinical comparison; Wiley full route redirects to abstract and references.

Abdian review abstracts saffron and isolated metabolites across many neurologic conditions including depression and PD, but does not isolate a ground-stigma PD depression outcome; publisher full body returned 403.
The Parkinson herbal review mentions saffron and sleep symptoms without an identified saffron insomnia study in the accessed abstract; retain original full-context gap.
The Parkinson herbal review names saffron and general motor rigidity but the accessible abstract does not identify a saffron rigidity comparison; full context remains inaccessible.
The Parkinson review mentions saffron and fatigue among separate broad examples; no source-specific saffron fatigue result can be verified without full body.
Alzheimer natural-products review lists Crocus among multiple plants and fatigue generally without linking a measured saffron fatigue endpoint; publisher requires PDF purchase.

English and Hebrew publisher abstracts assign cranberry to urinary infections and acupuncture to depression, without an identified cranberry depression result; original Hebrew body requires subscription or purchase.

Review abstract links rosemary to rosmarinic acid and reviews depression, Parkinson disease and other conditions. It does not present a fresh-rosemary depression estimate in the abstract; Springer shows subscription preview, and original cited experiments need full text to contextualize. Body access remains open.

Dopamine-agonist review mentions dyskinesia in drug context and ginger among possible nausea remedies. Abstract supplies no individual ginger-versus-control dyskinesia result; Springer preview references nausea review. Full original remains gated.

Scoping review includes 13 neurodegenerative studies and one ginger supplement, but abstract does not identify the ginger study population, preparation, results or individual report. Full review remains inaccessible; do not attribute this component to Parkinson disease.

Original synthesizes eugenol-derived compounds and tests enzyme inhibition and docking; discussion references anxiety broadly. No human oral ground-clove anxiety intervention or behavioral clinical result.

Published patent 1999-09-29 proposes isolated saponins/sapogenins from several plant genera including Asparagus for receptor and cognitive functions and lists chronic fatigue among putative conditions. No roasted asparagus participant exposure or measured fatigue comparison; fatigue also occurs in discussion of another drug's adverse effects.

Review lists grapes as source of stilbenes and describes resveratrol animal anxiety models; separate grape-seed extract is discussed for protein aggregation. It supplies no raw grape human Parkinson anxiety contrast.
Wild and hatchery brook trout genetic diversity study uses inbreeding depression in an ecological genetic sense, not human depressive symptoms or poached fish consumption.

Full-text Methods describe peanut oil as the oily-phase vehicle used to dissolve dopamine/soy lecithin in a self-nanoemulsifying delivery system; intervention is dopamine-loaded nanoparticles and bee venom in a reserpine PD rat model, not cold-pressed peanut oil. Fatigue is in the PD symptom background paragraph, not a measured endpoint. Candidate/exposure and symptom therefore do not form an oil/fatigue test.

The article is a systematic review of complement testing. “Rocket” is the lab method rocket immunoelectrophoresis (Table 2), not arugula/rocket food; fatigue occurs in a separate PNH symptom row (Table 3). No arugula exposure or fatigue intervention.
The original review lists peach as a source of ellagic acid and discusses Parkinson postural instability separately. It has no peach intervention or measured postural-instability association.

Full-text Methods use peanut oil only as vehicle for dopamine/soy-lecithin nanoemulsion; it is not a refined-peanut-oil treatment arm. Pain occurs in the PD symptom background, not as an outcome tested in this rat experiment. No evidence for refined peanut oil and pain severity.

Full-text narrative review Table 1 says a Mediterranean-diet intervention replaced several vegetable oils, including high-oleic sunflower oil, with extra-virgin olive oil; it summarizes ADAS-cog/global cognitive outcomes in older adults. This is not cold-pressed sunflower oil alone or a direct executive-function endpoint; candidate and target outcome arise in different evidence contexts.
Drosophila Parkinson-like model measures sleep fragmentation, but “Basil et al.” is an author citation (not fresh basil exposure). No basil intervention or insomnia-severity outcome.

Astaxanthin review notes astaxanthin occurs in trout and cites depression-related mouse work for astaxanthin in diabetic models; there is no poached-trout or human depression intervention/outcome. The ingredient and symptom are background in separate contexts.

Heavy-metals review lists rainbow trout among fish for monitoring food contamination, while depression is listed among neurological effects of arsenic exposure. No poached trout exposure or depression study; different hazards/contexts.

Article body covers DBS and mood/depression in Parkinson disease, but the captured full text contains no trout/food exposure. Archive-joined lexical ingredient flag is not supported by the local source text; treat as an indexing/join collision.

Oncology music-medicine review mentions trout only in an animal/livestock music table, while depression is an oncology symptom/intervention section. No trout diet or depressive symptom endpoint in people with Parkinson disease.

Older-adult cognitive-assessment review has Raspberry Pi (digital device) in a platform table, not raspberry fruit. Executive-function tests may occur among cognitive assessment domains but no raspberry intake/intervention is studied.

Nanomaterial/electrochemical sensing review mentions banana samples in an analytical validation example; dyskinesia is discussed as a risperidone/neurological drug adverse effect in a separate section. No raw-banana intake or PD dyskinesia outcome.

Neuromelanin/tyrosine-hydroxylase review notes banana plants synthesize dopamine; levodopa-induced dyskinesia appears in a separate PD mechanism discussion. No raw-banana intervention or dyskinesia outcome.
